title: Honolulu in late 1947: symphony, Lai Yi Chai's and Gibson's Bar
summary: He recounts going to Honolulu with C.P. Johnson's group, staying about three years, and writing an arrangement a day.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So I went to Honolulu, which just happened to come up... Because this is way before Trummy joined Louis. Jack Teagarden was still with him. So it was Trummy, Dexter Gordon, Ulysses Livingston, with Cee Pee Johnson (it was

his orchestra), and I can't remember the trumpet player's name... Anyway, we went to Honolulu. This was in the same year, 1947, late in the year. Trummy stayed in Honolulu until he joined Louis years later. But I think my total stay was about three years. I played in the Honolulu Symphony under Barati, and I had my own band in a place called Lai Yi Chai's, that was where Kalikawa meets (?) and Waikiki. Trummy had a band in the Brown Derby. I've already mentioned the names of the band somewhere back there, didn't I. Then I played in another place called Gibson's Bar with a smaller group.

Anyhow, that was fun. I already mentioned this. I used to do one arrangement a day, and that's how I built my library. These guys were just beautiful people to work with. it was the first time I'd worked with a real international band. They were good musicians, too.
